title: Set Matrix Zeroes
prompt: Given an `m x n` integer matrix, if an element is `0`, set its entire row and column to `0`, in place. Return the mutated matrix. Try to do it using `O(1)` extra space beyond the input and output.

examples.explanation: The single 0 at (1,1) zeroes out all of row 1 and all of column 1.
Zeroes at (0,0) and (0,3) each wipe out their row and column.
With no zero anywhere in the matrix, nothing changes.

hints: The naive approach copies the matrix to know which cells were originally 0 before mutating — that's O(mn) extra space. Can you avoid the copy?
You need to remember, for each row and column, whether it should be zeroed — what if you stored that information inside the matrix itself, using its first row and first column as markers?

Use matrix[0][j] and matrix[i][0] as flags for column j and row i respectively, but handle the first row/column's own zero-status separately with two boolean flags, since they double as both data and markers.

solution.approach: Instead of allocating separate row/column tracking arrays, reuse the matrix's own first row and first column as marker storage. First check with two booleans whether the first row and first column themselves originally contain a zero. Then scan the rest of the matrix (from row 1, col 1 onward): whenever a zero is found at (i, j), mark matrix[i][0] = 0 and matrix[0][j] = 0. After this pass, walk the matrix again (excluding the first row/column) and zero out any cell whose row-marker or column-marker is 0. Finally, zero out the first row and/or first column if the initial booleans indicated they should be. This achieves O(1) extra space beyond the input.
